_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce the risk of cardiovascular death and hospitalization for heart failure in patients with chronic heart failure (NYHA Class II-IV) and reduced ejection fraction

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: International, randomized, double-blind, double-dummy, parallel group, event-driven, active-controlled trial comparing LCZ696 (sacubitril/valsartan) with enalapril
pivotal_trials.population: Patients age ≥18 with NYHA class II to IV chronic heart failure and an LVEF ≤40% (≤35% per protocol amendment 1), on an ACE inhibitor or ARB and a beta-blocker
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary composite endpoint: time to first heart failure hospitalization or cardiovascular death
pivotal_trials.result: Primary composite endpoint occurred in 914 (21.8%) LCZ696 vs 1117 (26.5%) enalapril (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.73, 0.87; 1-sided p=0.0000002). All-cause mortality: HR 0.84 (95% CI 0.76, 0.93; 2-sided p=0.0009).

key_safety: Adverse reactions occurring ≥5% are hypotension (18% vs 12% enalapril), hyperkalemia (12% vs 14%), cough (9% vs 13%), dizziness (6% vs 5%), and renal failure (5% vs 5%). Angioedema occurred in 0.5% of ENTRESTO vs 0.2% enalapril (2.4% vs 0.5% in Black patients).
target_moa: ENTRESTO inhibits neprilysin (neutral endopeptidase) via LBQ657, the active metabolite of the prodrug sacubitril, and blocks the angiotensin II type-1 (AT1) receptor via valsartan
modality: Small molecule (fixed-dose combination of sacubitril, a neprilysin inhibitor, and valsartan, an angiotensin II receptor blocker)

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: FETAL TOXICITY — When pregnancy is detected, discontinue ENTRESTO as soon as possible; drugs that act directly on the renin-angiotensin system can cause injury and death to the developing fetus

advisory_committee.vote: No Advisory Committee Meeting was held; there were no significant safety and/or efficacy issues requiring Advisory Committee input

description.text: Added indication for treatment of symptomatic heart failure with systemic left ventricular systolic dysfunction in pediatric patients aged one year and older

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application, submitted in response to a Pediatric Written Request, supports a labeled indication for use of Entresto® for treatment of symptomatic heart failure with systemic left ventricular systolic dysfunction in pediatric patients aged one year and older. Entresto® reduces NT-proBNP and is expected to improve cardiovascular outcomes.

description.text: Revised Indications and Usage based on the PARAGON-HF trial (broadening use in chronic heart failure)

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for updates to the United States Prescribing Information (USPI) and the Patient Package Insert (PPI) related to the PARAGON-HF trial, including substantive revisions to Indications and Usage and Clinical Studies; additional revisions were made throughout labeling.

summary.text: ENTRESTO was approved on the basis of the single phase 3 PARADIGM-HF trial after the Agency granted fast track designation, rolling review and priority review; the application was approved first cycle with no Advisory Committee meeting and no accelerated approval.

citations.quote: In April 2014, Novartis notified the Agency that the Data Monitoring Committee for their phase 3 trial had recommended early closure for compelling efficacy. The Agency subsequently granted fast track designation, rolling review and priority review.

In support of the proposed indication, the applicant conducted a single phase 3 trial, PARADIGM-HF. requirement.text: 2924-2: A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial to evaluate the effects of Entresto compared to valsartan on cognitive function in patients with chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction

citations.quote: 2924-2 A multicenter, randomized, double-blind, active-controlled trial to evaluate the effects of Entresto compared to valsartan on cognitive function as assessed by comprehensive neurocognitive battery and PET imaging in patients with chronic heart failure with preserved ejection fraction.

requirement.text: 2924-3: Development of a new dissolution method for all strengths with demonstrated discriminating ability and setting of the final dissolution acceptance criterion for Entresto Tablets (97/103, 49/51, and 24/26 mg)

citations.quote: 2924-3 Development of a new dissolution method for all the strengths with demonstrated discriminating ability, (b)(4), and setting of the final dissolution acceptance criterion for Entresto™ (sacubitril/valsartan) Tablets, 97/103, 49/51, and 24/26 mg using the new dissolution method and data from the overall multipoint dissolution profile from a minimum of 12 commercial batches per strength, manufactured under the same conditions as those used for the manufacture of the batches used in pivotal clinical trials. The FDA will be open to providing feedback during the method's development process as needed.
